## 3. Red flags

### 1. [HIGH] No weekly rest day or holiday pay

The contract says there is no weekly rest day (주휴일). Workers who work 15 hours or more per week are entitled to a paid weekly rest day (주휴수당).

> Korean: 5.근무일/휴일:매주월,화,수,목,금요일근무/주휴일:없음  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 2. [HIGH] Hourly wage below the legal minimum

The hourly wage is 9,000 KRW. The legal minimum wage is 10,320 KRW per hour in 2026. Paying less is not allowed, even if you agree to it. Ask for a correction or contact the Ministry of Employment and Labor (call 1350).

> Korean: -시간급:9,000원  (quote matched to scan: yes)

- [ ] real problem  - [ ] not a problem (false alarm)  - [ ] explanation correct  - [ ] severity right

### 3. [HIGH] No social insurance

The employer does not enrol the worker in social insurance (national pension, health, employment, accident). Employers must do this for most workers, and missing insurance can also cause problems with your visa and health care.

> Korean: 8.사회보험 적용여부: 고용보험[]산재보험[] 국민연금[] 건강보험[](가입하지 않음)  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 4. [HIGH] You do not get a copy of the contract

The employer must give you a copy of the signed contract (Labor Standards Act, article 17). Without a copy you cannot prove the wage, hours or duties. Ask for a signed copy, or take a photo of every page before you leave.

> Korean: 9.근로계약서교부: 본계약서는 사업주가 보관하며 근로자에게 교부하지 않는다  (quote matched to scan: yes)

### 5. [HIGH] The employer holds a deposit from you

The employer asks you to leave a deposit and decides alone whether to return it. Employers generally may not take money from a worker as a guarantee or penalty (Labor Standards Act, articles 20 and 22). Do not hand over cash without a receipt, and ask a labor office (1350) before you agree.

### 6. [MEDIUM] No overtime or night pay

The contract says overtime, night or holiday work is not paid extra. The law requires 50% extra pay for overtime, night work (22:00 to 06:00) and holiday work at workplaces with 5 or more employees. Saying it is 'included' in the hourly wage is not valid unless the wage clearly covers it.

Cash payment leaves no record. Ask for a payslip or a bank transfer, because you need proof of income and of the hours you worked.

### 8. [MEDIUM] Costs are taken out of your wages

The contract lets the employer deduct the cost of a uniform or broken items from your wages. Wages must generally be paid in full (Labor Standards Act, article 43), so such deductions are usually not allowed. Ask for it to be removed.
